comment: I volunteer at Hildegarde's Food Pantry, a food pantry organized and supported by St. Marks Episcopal Cathedral. It has been a challenge to maintain the pantry this year due to the variety of challenges posed by the Covid pandemic. The Street Ambassadors have been instrumental in the smooth operation of the pantry. Their presence has brought order out of chaos. Due to the large homeless population that gathers on the parking strip, we needed the Street Ambassadors support to provide our patrons with the assurance that their safety was not at risk. I would urge the council to continue to fund this important service to our community. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r1JXhSYfLNE These have been around for sometime, why not use them. It seems to be a simple answer for a complex problem. Mike

I really hope we don't lose this spot. My brother is one of the many heartbreaking lives taken from us, he is one of the many murals on the building. The day Joey Tucker was murdered was the worst day of my life, changed me forever. It never gets easier, ever!!! I love the murals, our loved ones are not forgotten, we have a peaceful place to visit them, share their stories. We have formed new friendships through the darkest time in our lives. I'm so grateful to the artists, everyone who has helped us so our loved ones aren't forgotten, to those who lend a listening ear or shoulder to cry on. Please dont let hs lose these murals.

I represent Wonderbloom which is a preschool located at 231 E 100 S in Salt Lake City. We have experienced an increase in loitering, homeless encampments, property damage, and harassment in the last 6 months. Several times a week, we call on the Downtown Ambassadors to help us with these issues. They are always quick to respond and deal with the situation - often arriving within 5 minutes. We feel safe running a preschool downtown because the Ambassadors are so responsive. In fact, last month a man high on drugs attempted to violently break into the preschool while children and staff were present. We sheltered in place and called 911 right away. After 15 minutes when the police failed to show up, we called the Downtown Ambassadors. They came within 15 minutes, arriving before the police, and let us know that there was no longer a threat and we could let the children out from the Shelter-in-place location. Please expand funding for the Downtown Ambassadors. They are crucial in keeping the young children safe in their downtown preschool.

Council Members, I am a constituent here in Salt Lake City and a member of the community. I live between Liberty Park and the Fleet Block. I strongly oppose the rezoning of this block. As you know, the Fleet Block is home to a collection of murals which honor those killed by police violence. The murals have served as a gathering space for the community since the first one was painted. In this space, people pray, protest, mourn, collect donations, and meet with each other. The community has planted flowers in this space and beautified the entire block. Because of all of this, I believe this block is more beneficial and important to the community as-is, than it would be as a "redeveloped" block of offices or apartments. This space does not need redeveloping as it is safe, pleasant, and community-oriented as-is. Thank you for your time. I hope you will put the needs of the current community over the money of developers. Laurel Clayson

I work at a preschool downtown, and the street ambassadors are the most amazing people who keep us safe everyday. They always respond to calls very quickly about people on our property, and they check in with us every morning. they go above and beyond to help us feel safe. And not only that, but they always have the best interest of those living on the streets and WANT to help them. It makes me feel good calling them knowing that the person I called about is in good non-violent hands.
